articles.summary: A medical canvass can come back with no hits for a few reasons: the claimant was never treated there, the facility refused or required a HIPAA release, or the canvasser didn't try hard enough. Why canvasses miss, the test every no-hit should pass, and what a defensible result looks like.
articles.title: Why Your Medical Canvass Came Back With No Hits (and How to Tell a Real Negative From a Refusal)

articles.summary: No single source verifies every applicant, so lenders and screeners run a waterfall: database first, payroll link second, employer outreach last. How the tiers work, where each one fails, what the fallback tier costs, and the design decisions that decide your completion rate.
articles.title: The Employment Verification Waterfall: Database First, Manual Fallback

articles.summary: ISO ClaimSearch is Verisk's database of more than 1.8 billion U.S. P&C claims, covering roughly 95% of the market. Here is what a match report shows, who can access it, what it costs, what it can't tell an SIU, and where a medical canvass picks up.
articles.title: What Is ISO ClaimSearch? How the Insurance Claims Database Works

articles.summary: TPAs run medical canvassing differently from carriers: it's a billable service, ordered across many client brands, and often subcontracted to vendors who white-label the report. What TPA SIU teams told us about volume, cycle time, and the three problems that keep coming up, plus a canvass protocol built for TPA work.
articles.title: Medical Canvassing for TPAs: How Third-Party Administrators Run It, Price It, and Scale It
